title: France – Urban planning and landscape architectural services – Accord cadre de maîtrise d'oeuvre urbaine et opérationnelle pour la ZAC du Pré Gauchet à Nantes
description: Le projet urbain du Pré Gauchet s'étend sur un territoire de 164 ha à proximité immédiate du centre-ville de Nantes, entre la Gare au Nord et la Loire au Sud. Depuis 2003 Nantes Métropole et Nantes Métropole Aménagement y conduisent une opération de renouvellement urbain visant à : désenclaver le quartier de Malakoff par la construction d'infrastructures permettant de le relier au centre-ville et à l'île de Nantes, et par le développement d'un nouveau quartier à vivre, mixte, au pied de la gare ; participer au développement d'un pôle tertiaire : EuroNantes, en construisant près de 170 000 m²SP de bureaux sur le secteur. Aujourd'hui, le projet urbain conçu par le Groupement Ruelle architecture (mandataire)a déjà vu se construire 1700 logements, 145 000 m² de bureaux, 17 000 m² d'activités, 60 000 m² d'équipements. Les espaces publics structurants sont également déjà réalisés, à savoir le mail Pablo Picasso, le boulevard de Berlin, la rue Marcel Paul, le parvis de la Gare sud. Le projet en est à sa dernière étape, comprenant : La mise en oeuvre opérationnelle du dernier secteur constitué des îlots situés gare sud, face au PEM livré en 2025 ; La mise en oeuvre des îlots SAUPIN, E et 3C ; Le suivi des opérations en diffus à l'échelle de la ZAC ; La réalisation de la voie cyclable Magistrale sur le mail Pablo Picasso. L'équipe de maîtrise d'oeuvre devra également s'investir sur tous les sujets connexes aux objets d'ores et déjà identifiés (accompagnements divers de toutes les initiatives qui surviennent) et aux thématiques transversales qui doivent être portées aux côtés de la maîtrise d'ouvrage : travail sur les rez-de-chaussée, travail sur les continuités paysagères… L'accompagnement des projets immobiliers devra se faire dans la continuité du travail mené jusqu'à présent, mettant en avant l'excellence architecturale et le lien entre l'espace public et les rez-de-chaussée. La conception des espaces publics devra quant à elle, poursuivre sa contribution à l'infiltration des eaux pluviales, la climatisation de la ville, l'accueil de la biodiversité. Elle oeuvrera également à favoriser les mobilités actives, le bien être au travail et chez soi, la convivialité et la recherche de lien social. Le périmètre, les enjeux et objectifs de l'opération sont présentés dans la Note de présentation et ses annexes ; l'ensemble de ces documents sont téléchargeables sur le profil d'acheteur.

title: Denmark – Construction work – Udbud af modnings- og bygningsentreprise i forbindelse med etablering af Vestsjælland Arrest
description: Nærværende udbud vedrører indgåelse af en storentreprisekontrakt for modnings- og bygningsarbejder i forbindelse med etablering af Vestsjælland Arrest. Udbuddet gennemføres som udbud med forhandling efter offentliggørelse af en udbudsbekendtgørelse, jf. Forsvars- og Sikkerhedsdirektivets art. 26 (Direktiv 2009/81/EF af 13. juli 2009), og omfatter således en tilbudsfase, hvor kun prækvalificerede ansøgere har mulighed for at afgive indledende tilbud. Danmarks Fængsler skal etablere en ny arrest ved Slagelse. Arresten skal være en moderne og tidssvarende institution med arrest- og afsoningspladser i en fleksibel struktur, med tryghed og sikkerhed, der understøtter effektive arbejdsgange til gavn for både ansatte, indsatte og besøgende. Arresten etableres i et landbrugslandskab med marker som naboer mod nord og øst, mens der mod vest findes mindre landbrugsbygninger og private boliger og haver. Arresten etableres på et areal på ca. 34 Ha og i et relativt kuperet terræn. Inden for det angivne projektområde er terrænet kuperet med over 28 m difference mellem højeste og laveste punkt. Bygningerne etableres i en til to etager, placeres spredt på grunden, koblet sammen af et vej- og stisystem. Bygningernes samlede etageareal er ca. 46.000 m2. Arrestens struktur er fordelt på følgende hovedfunktioner: port- og varefunktioner,belægsafdelinger, særligt sikret belægsbygning, fællesfunktioner (herunder beskæftigelse, sundheds- og fritidsfaciliteter), personalefunktioner og støttefunktioner. Der henvises i øvrigt til Bilag 1 for en nærmere projektbeskrivelse. Byggeriet udbydes i to storentrepriser: én modnings- og bygningsentreprise og én sikringsentreprise. Nærværende udbud omhandler modnings- og bygningsentreprisen. Den udbudte kontrakt er ikke opdelt i delaftaler. Ordregiver har, med baggrund i økonomiske- og markedsmæssige hensyn, vurderet, at det ikke er hensigtsmæssigt at foretage en sådan opdeling. Projektet og relevante oplysninger til brug for ansøgere til prækvalifikation, er overordnet beskrevet i prækvalifikationsmaterialet, som er tilgængeligt for ansøgere via følgende link: https://node1.field.dalux.com/service/redirect/client/ten/TID-465823455586035472/da-dk/public/tender/TID-465823455586035472. Prækvalifikationsmaterialet består af følgende dokumenter: Nærværende udbudsbekendtgørelse, Udbudsbetingelserne, Følgende bilag til udbudsbetingelserne: - Bilag A: Egnethedsvurderingen - Bilag A1: Støtteerklæring vedr. andre enheders økonomiske formåen - Bilag A2: Støtteerklæring vedr. andre enheders tekniske formåen - Bilag A3: Konsortieerklæring - Bilag A4: Tro- og loveerklæring vedr. russiske leverandører og underleverandører - Bilag A5: Ansøgningsbetingelser til prækvalifikation - Bilag A6: Referenceskabelon - Bilag A7: Sikkerhedshåndteringsmanual - Bilag A8: Erklæring om tavshedspligt og Samtykkeerklæring - Bilag A9: Skabelon for oversigter over personer der skal have adgang til udbudsmateriale, ESPD, Bilag 1: Projektbeskrivelse. Det samlede udbudsmateriale vil blive gjort tilgængeligt via Dalux for de ansøgere, der bliver udvalgt til at afgive tilbud.

description: Achiziție publică de servicii de dezvoltare platformă Metaverse și implementare sistem de management de tip Digital Twin pentru Hub-ul infrastructurii DANUBIUS-RI, în cadrul Proiectului cu acronim DANUBIUS-RO-2, Contract de finanțare pentru Programul 5.9 Cercetare în domenii de interes strategic, Subprogramul 5.9.4 Sistemele fluvii, delte, mări- DANUBIUS din cadrul Planului Național de Cercetare, Dezvoltare și Inovare 2022-2027, nr. 1D din 03.10.2025. Institutul Național de Cercetare – Dezvoltare pentru Științe Biologice București (INCDSB) coordonează la nivel național proiectul DANUBIUS-RO prin care se finanteaza constructia si operationalizarea componentelor romanesti ale infrastructurii pan-europene DANUBIUS-RI: Hub-ul si Supersite-ul Delta Dunarii. DANUBIUS-RO se constituie ca o rețea complexă de laboratoare, stații de teren și puncte de observație destinate monitorizării mediului marin, costier și fluvial, cu accent pe zonele de interes strategic precum Delta Dunării, litoralul Mării Negre și sectorul inferior al Dunării. Dezvoltarea continuă a infrastructurii de cercetare prin proiectele de cercetare aplicată derulate de INCDSB și partenerii săi in arealul Biosfera Delta Dunarii – inclusiv în cadrul programelor naționale și europene dedicate monitorizării riscurilor naturale, protecției mediului și adaptării la schimbările climatice – impune o atentie deosebita a sustenabilitatii si rezilientei ansamblului de cladiri aferente Hub-ului de la Murighiol. Aceasta trebuie să susțină fluxuri tot mai mari de date științifice, imagini și măsurători complexe provenite din teren, în vederea transmiterii lor către centrele de procesare și analiză din Murighiol, Tulcea, Galați, Constanța și București. În contextul extinderii rețelei de puncte de observație și al creșterii volumului de informații generate de echipamentele de monitorizare și cercetare, a devenit necesară modernizarea infrastructurii de procesare integrată a datelor colectate. Prin urmare, este necesară achiziția de servicii de Dezvoltare a platformei de tip Metaverse și implementarea unui sistem de management de tip Digital Twin pentru Hub-ul infrastructurii DANUBIUS-RI, permițând integrarea unitară a datelor colectate în cadrul laboratoarelor Hub-ului si activităților aferente Supersite-ului Delta Dunării de monitorizare a mediului marin și fluvial, a riscurilor geodinamice și a proceselor de eroziune costieră. Această infrastructură va contribui la îmbunătățirea capabilităților de analiză, avertizare timpurie și suport decizional, consolidând rolul INCDSB și al partenerilor instituționali în gestionarea durabilă a resurselor și în organizarea eficientă a ecosistemelor de cercetare de importanță națională și europeană.

description: The United States Coast Guard Academy has a requirement for the replacement in kind of an existing folding accordion-style door at the Consolidated Club, located at 15 Mohegan Drive, New London, Connecticut. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, tools, equipment, supervision, transportation, and incidentals necessary to remove and properly dispose of the existing accordion door assembly, including tracks, hardware, and associated mounting components, and furnish and install a new hardwood cherry veneer accordion-style partition door. The replacement door shall include matching side attachments, a center-opening configuration, all required tracks, rollers, hinges, guides, latches, hardware, and fasteners, and shall fit the existing opening of approximately 6 feet 10 inches high by 15 feet wide without modifying the existing structure or opening. The contractor shall verify field conditions prior to fabrication or installation and leave the work area clean upon completion.

title: Replace Garage Doors
description: The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, tools, supervision, transportation, and incidentals necessary to remove and replace two existing garage doors at the Grounds Storage Building, Coast Guard Academy, New London, Connecticut. The work includes removal and offsite disposal of the existing doors, tracks, hardware, fasteners, and associated components; furnishing and installing two new white flush-panel glazed garage doors of the same size and configuration, including new tracks, rollers, hinges, brackets, cables, torsion springs, bearings, mounting hardware, weather seals, locks, and related operating components; verifying existing framing and mounting surfaces; aligning, leveling, balancing, lubricating, and testing the doors for proper operation; and demonstrating proper operation to the Government upon completion. All work shall be performed in accordance with manufacturer instructions, applicable building codes, OSHA safety requirements, and industry standards, and the completed doors shall be fully operational, securely mounted, weather-tight, and free of defects.

title: Stage 1 -Amishku-Shipiss-Kigiap Konga - Beaver Brook Camp-Akami−Uapishkᵘ−KakKasuak−Mealy Mountains National Park Reserve
description: 5P468-26-0151/A Stage 1 -Amishku-Shipiss-Kigiap Konga - Beaver Brook Camp-Akami-Uapishk?-KakKasuak-Mealy Mountains National Park Reserve BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS TO BIDDERS (SI) This is a two stage selection process. Bidders responding to this selection process are requested to submit a bid in two stages. This posting is the first stage (Stage One) of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage will evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers; the second stage (Stage Two) will invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Upon award of contract in Stage Two the pre-qualification list will expire and will not be used in any other solicitation. The qualification list will expire within 180 days or upon award of a contract in Stage Two, whichever is earlier, and the prequalification list will not be used in any other solicitation. Following the evaluation of the submissions of Stage One, bidders will be advised of their qualification result and the status of the tender. Parks Canada reserves the right to re-issue Stage One via a /B solicitation if it is determined there is insufficient competition to proceed with Stage Two. Bidders that have qualified in Stage One /A will not be required to resubmit on the Stage One /B. Bidders that failed to demonstrate compliance on the Stage One /A may resubmit and will be considered in Stage One /B. Stage Two Bidders will be provided an INVITATION TO TENDER (ITT) for further qualifications and the financial evaluation in relation to the specifications and drawings. Please note that the ITT used in Stage 2 of this process will be a Two-Envelope ITT with a mandatory Indigenous Participation Plan (IPP) and a price evaluation component. LIST OF PRE-QUALIFIED BIDDERS: A list of pre-qualified bidders from Stage One will not be released. Contract award notice of the successful bidder of Stage Two will be posted on http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities PARTNER WITH ANOTHER BUSINESS: Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business” REQUIREMENT The Beaver Brook Camp project involves the complete construction of a camp facility located at the junction of Lake Melville and Etagaulet River, in Newfoundland and Labrador (Approx. coordinates are: 53°42'56.37"N 59°01'06.20"W). The Camp is comprised of 3 buildings, a Lodge (69m2 with a 34m2 screen porch and deck), a Privy (Backcountry Toilet, approx. 18m2) and a Cache (Storage Shed, approx. 25m2), all linked through wooden boardwalks (approx. 250m of boardwalks) and powered through solar panels. Tent Pads (five (5) total), a food cache, a seasonal floating dock, log benches, picnic tables, fire pit and a traditional camping site are also included in this project. Overall site work, tree clearing, topsoil preservation and re-naturalization, is required for this site. The site is remote with no existing infrastructure and is only accessible by boat, seaplane, helicopter or by snowmobile (during winter-pending safe ice conditions). Full project details, including drawings and specifications, will be provided to qualified bidders in Stage Two. To assist with bonding and insurance requirements, this project is estimated at a value between $2,500,001 > $5,000,000, Taxes extra. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than November 30, 2027 COMPREHENSIVE LAND CLAIMS AGREEMENT This procurement is subject to the following comprehensive Land Claims Agreement(s): • Labrador Inuit Land Claims Agreement • the Labrador Inuit Park Impacts and Benefits Agreement and • the Innu Nation Park Impacts and Benefits Agreement. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. title: Syötteen LumiAreenan operaattorin valinta (käyttöoikeus) v. 2027-2029 (-2030-2031)
description: Syötteen LumiAreenan operaattorin valinta (käyttöoikeus) v. 2027-2029 (-2030-2031) Pudasjärven kaupunki omistaa Syötteellä LumiAreena -tapahtuma- ja liikunta-areenan. Kohde on otettu käyttöön vuonna 2019. Nykyinen varaus- ja vuokraustoiminnan operointisopimus päättyy 31.12.2026. Tuloja tuottava areenan tapahtuma- ja liikuntakäyttö ovat jääneet verrattain vähäisiksi. Kaupunki tunnistaa LumiAreenan merkityksen Syötteen ja koko kaupungin matkailun kehittämiselle, ja kaupunki on sitoutunut toimintaan ja sen kehittämiseen. Kohteella arvioidaan olevan kaupallista potentiaalia, mutta samalla on tunnistettu että potentiaalin hyödyntäminen edellyttänee merkittäviä muutoksia areenan operointiin. Uuden toimintamallin valmisteluun on osallistettu yrittäjiä. Uusi toimija valitaan julkisella kilpailutuksella (käyttöoikeussopimus) 3 vuoden sopimuskaudeksi, jota voidaan jatkaa kahdella yhden vuoden mittaisella optiokaudella (3+1+1). Areenan yläkerrassa olevat liiketilat ja areenan alakerrassa oleva kuntosali ovat käytössä ja muodostavat toimivan kokonaisuuden, eivätkä kyseiset tilat kuulu operointisopimuksen piiriin. Uusi malli tarkoitta areenan vuokraamista valitulle yrittäjälle, jolloin vuokraustoiminta tapahtuisi yrittäjän lukuun 1.1.2027 alkaen seuraavasti: - Operaattori saa: - käyttöoikeuden areenan saliin, yläkerran (ylätason) aulatilaan (aulatilasta kulku myös liiketiloihin), wc-tiloihin, siivoustiloihin, areenan salin yhteydessä olevaan varastoon. (Lisätietoja: Tällä hetkellä areenan salin käyttöä suljettuihin kokouksiin/tilaisuuksiin haastaa, että yläkerran aulatilan (jossa myös liiketilat) ja areenan välillä on vain verho. Tämä ei ollut ongelma esimerkiksi keikkakäytössä, jolloin yläkerran aulatilassa toimii narikka ja koska keikka-ajankohtina yläkerran liiketilat eivät käytännössä ole avoinna, jolloin ulkopuolisten pääsy voidaan estää myös yläkerran aulatilaan. Todennäköisesti mahdollisuus käyttää kokousta myös suljettuihin kokouksiin on kuitenkin operaattorille kaupallisesti tärkeä. Tältä osin kilpailutuksessa käytetään optiomenettelyä, jossa perusvaihtoehdon (teknisiä muutoksia em. seikan osalta ei toteuteta), pyydetään tarjoamaan optiona hinta vaihtoehdolle, jossa tilaaja (kaupunki) toteuttaa ennen sopimuskauden alkamista väliseinän yläaulan ja areenan salin välille. Toisena toimintaa rajoittavana tekijänä on havaittu lämpimän varastotilan puute, sillä salin yhteydessä oleva varasto on pieni ja täynnä salin kalustamiseen soveltuvia kalusteita, liikuntavälineitä ja AV/PA-tekniikkaa. Tämä vaikeuttaa säännöllisessä käytössä (esim. anniskelu) tarvittavan materiaalin varastointia. Tältäkin osin kilpailutuksessa käytetään optiomenettelyä, jossa perusvaihtoehdon (teknisiä muutoksia em. seikan osalta ei toteuteta), pyydetään tarjoamaan optiona hinta vaihtoehdolle ,jossa tilaaja (kaupunki) toteuttaa ennen sopimuskauden alkamista vähintään 10 nelimetrin kokoisen lämpimän lisävarastotilan (esim. kontti) areenan salin läheisyyteen. Lisätietoja kohteesta, mm. suuntaa-antava pohjakuva liitteenä olevasta LumiAreenan esitteestä (sis. osittain vanhentunutta tietoa). Sivulla 3 olevassa Ylätason pohjakuvassa oleva Monikäyttösali-niminen tila muunnettu siten, että valtaosan siitä vievät liiketilat, jotka eivät kuulu operointisopimuksen piiriin. Sisäänkäynti areenan saliin ja narikka mahtuvat kuitenkin toimimaan em. tilan vapaissa ja operaattorin käyttöön tulevissa tiloissa. Lisätietoja LumiAreenasta myös kaupungin verkkosivuilta osoitteesta https://www.pudasjarvi.fi/liikuntapalvelut/sisaliikuntapaikat/lumiareena/) - kaikki areenan vuokratulot; hinnoittelusta päättää operaattori - Operaattori voi myydä vuokraan sisältyen tai tai lisäpalveluina muita toimintaan liittyviä palveluita kuten aulapalveluita, AV-tukea esitystekniikkaan, muita kokouspalveluita, ateriapalveluita ja/tai anniskelua - Operaattori myy kohdetta kuin omaansa, mikä mahdollistaa myös integroinnin operaattorin muuhun markkinointiin/myyntiin. Operaattori vastaa/maksaa: - kilpailutuksessa tarjoamansa kuukausikorvauksen - areenan siivouksen ml. saniteettituotteet - tilojen käytöstä tilaisuuksissa suoraan aiheutuvat kustannukset pois lukien esiintymislavan rakentamisesta ja purkamisesta sekä liikuntakäyttöön tarkoitetun lattiapinnan muun käytön ajaksi peittämisestä ja purkamisesta aiheutuvat kiinteistöhuollon kustannukset - toiminnan edellyttämät vakuutukset (vähintään vastuuvakuutus, tarvittaessa operaattorin oman toiminnan vakuutukset) Areenan omistaja (kaupunki) vastaa/maksaa: - muut kulut, mm. sähkö, lämpö, vesi, kiinteistöhuolto, jätehuolto, vartiointi, rakennuksen vakuutukset - liikuntakäytön edellyttämien pukuhuoneiden käyttöoikeuden järjestäminen operaattorille (areenan vieressä olevat pukuhuoneet on vuokrattu muulle toimijalle) - ohjaus linkillä kaupungin verkkosivuilta operaattorin verkkosivuille - perehdytyksen kohteen AV-laitteisiin - perehdytyksen kohteen turvallisuusasioihin Kilpailutuksessa kysytään korvauksen määrää (alv 0), jonka tarjoaja tarjoaa kaupungille kuukaudessa (alv 0). Valintaperusteena on pisteytys siten, että perushinnan painoarvo on 85 % ja optioiden sisältävien hintojen painoarvot 5 % (väliseinä toteutetaan), 5 % (lisävarastotila toteutetaan) ja 5 % (sekä väliseinä että lisävarastotila toteutetaan). Mitä suurempia ovat tarjotut hinnat, sitä korkeampi on pisteytys. Operaattorin valinta tehdään syksyllä 2026, jotta operaattori voi aloittaa markkinoinnin/myynnin 1.1.2027 alkavasta ajankohdasta eteenpäin. HUOM! Tilaaja päättää hankintapäätöksen tehdessään, valitseeko se kilpailutuksen voittajalta perustarjouksen vai jonkun optioista sisältävän vaihtoehdon. Tarjoaja voi pyrkiä varmistamaan väliseinän ja/tai lisävarastotilan toteuttamisen ja tältä osin areenan paremman hyödynnettävyyden tarjoamalla näissä vaihtoehdossa niin paljon perushintaa paremman hinnan, että tilaaja päätyy toteuttamaan muutostyön/muutostyöt.,

title: AE TITLE II/PCAS Repair of Storm Sewer Water and Sanitary Sewer Systems, Caserma Miotto, Longare, Vicenza, Italy.
description: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole-Source Contract Subject: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole-Source Contract for Post Construction Award Services (PCAS) for the Caserma Miotto Storm and Sanitary Project. Agency: 414th Contracting Support Brigade (CSB), Regional Contracting Office (RCO) Vicenza, Italy. Description: The 414th CSB intends to negotiate and award a sole-source contract to A.I.C.E. Consulting Srl for the provision of Title II / Post Construction Award Services (PCAS) for the Caserma Miotto Storm and Sanitary Project in Longare, Italy. Description of Services: The required services include comprehensive construction oversight to ensure the project is executed in strict accordance with the original design specifications. This includes, but is not limited to, conducting on-site inspections, reviewing and approving technical submittals from the construction contractor, responding to Requests for Information (RFIs), resolving unforeseen site conditions, and providing final certification of the completed works. These services are critical for ensuring the quality, safety, and compliance of a major infrastructure project. Statutory Authority: This action is being executed on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1 "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." Justification for Sole-Source Award: A.I.C.E. Consulting Srl is the original Designer of Record (DoR) for the Caserma Miotto Storm and Sanitary Project. Under established engineering protocols and federal procurement guidelines, awarding the follow-on PCAS contract to the DoR is essential for the following reasons: Continuity of Knowledge: As the DoR, A.I.C.E. possesses unique, proprietary, and non-transferable technical familiarity with the complex engineering calculations, site-specific design adaptations, and overall design intent. Only the DoR can seamlessly provide the required oversight without introducing significant risks. Prevention of Substantial Duplication of Costs: Awarding this contract to any other firm would legally require the new entity to conduct an exhaustive, independent review and re-validation of the entire original design in order to assume professional liability. This would force the Government to pay a second time for engineering analysis already performed, representing a substantial duplication of cost that is not expected to be recovered through competition. Avoidance of Unacceptable Delays: The construction phase of this project is imminent. A new competitive action would require a minimum of 120 days for procurement, plus additional weeks or months for a new firm to familiarize themselves with the design. Such a delay would halt a critical $12.4M life-safety project, leaving failing infrastructure exposed and resulting in serious harm to the Government's mission. Therefore, the Government has determined that A.I.C.E. Consulting Srl is the only responsible source capable of performing these highly specialized services without causing unacceptable delays and a substantial duplication of costs. Instructions to Interested Parties: This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources who believe they can meet the Government's requirements as the Designer of Record may submit a capability statement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action is solely within the discretion of the Government. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Capability statements must be submitted via email to Contracting Officer Daniel Veenstra (email: daniel.l.veenstra.civ@army.mil) and Contracting Specialist Jimmy Amaya (email: jimmy.j.amaya.civ@army.mil) no later than 15:00 PM CEST, on 1 September 2026. Phone calls will not be accepted. Product Service Code: C211 - ARCHITECT AND ENGINEERING- GENERAL: LANDSCAPING, INTERIOR LAYOUT, AND DESIGNING NAICS Code: 541330 - Engineering Services Place of Performance: Caserma Miotto, Longare, Vicenza, Italy.

description: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole-Source Contract Subject: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole-Source Contract for Post Construction Award Services (PCAS) for the Caserma Miotto Storm and Sanitary Project. Agency: 414th Contracting Support Brigade (CSB), Regional Contracting Office (RCO) Vicenza, Italy. Description: The 414th CSB intends to negotiate and award a sole-source contract to A.I.C.E. Consulting Srl for the provision of Title II / Post Construction Award Services (PCAS) for the Caserma Miotto Storm and Sanitary Project in Longare, Italy. Description of Services: The required services include comprehensive construction oversight to ensure the project is executed in strict accordance with the original design specifications. This includes, but is not limited to, conducting on-site inspections, reviewing and approving technical submittals from the construction contractor, responding to Requests for Information (RFIs), resolving unforeseen site conditions, and providing final certification of the completed works. These services are critical for ensuring the quality, safety, and compliance of a major infrastructure project. Statutory Authority: This action is being executed on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1 "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." Justification for Sole-Source Award: A.I.C.E. Consulting Srl is the original Designer of Record (DoR) for the Caserma Miotto Storm and Sanitary Project. Under established engineering protocols and federal procurement guidelines, awarding the follow-on PCAS contract to the DoR is essential for the following reasons: Continuity of Knowledge: As the DoR, A.I.C.E. possesses unique, proprietary, and non-transferable technical familiarity with the complex engineering calculations, site-specific design adaptations, and overall design intent. Only the DoR can seamlessly provide the required oversight without introducing significant risks. Prevention of Substantial Duplication of Costs: Awarding this contract to any other firm would legally require the new entity to conduct an exhaustive, independent review and re-validation of the entire original design in order to assume professional liability. This would force the Government to pay a second time for engineering analysis already performed, representing a substantial duplication of cost that is not expected to be recovered through competition. Avoidance of Unacceptable Delays: The construction phase of this project is imminent. A new competitive action would require a minimum of 120 days for procurement, plus additional weeks or months for a new firm to familiarize themselves with the design. Such a delay would halt a critical $12.4M life-safety project, leaving failing infrastructure exposed and resulting in serious harm to the Government's mission. Therefore, the Government has determined that A.I.C.E. Consulting Srl is the only responsible source capable of performing these highly specialized services without causing unacceptable delays and a substantial duplication of costs. Instructions to Interested Parties: This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources who believe they can meet the Government's requirements as the Designer of Record may submit a capability statement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action is solely within the discretion of the Government. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Capability statements must be submitted via email to Contracting Officer Stacey Miller (email: stacey.l.miller45.civ@army.mil) and Contracting Specialist Jimmy Amaya (email: jimmy.j.amaya.civ@army.mil) no later than 15:00 PM CEST, on 1 September 2026. Phone calls will not be accepted. Product Service Code: C211 - ARCHITECT AND ENGINEERING- GENERAL: LANDSCAPING, INTERIOR LAYOUT, AND DESIGNING NAICS Code: 541330 - Engineering Services Place of Performance: Caserma Miotto, Longare, Vicenza, Italy.

title: ACCELERATING RATE CALORIMETER (ARC) SYSTEM
description: The National Research Council Canada (NRC) is seeking offers from Offerors to provide a high-precision Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC) system to support the safety and thermal characterization of advanced energy storage technologies to the National Research Council Canada. All deliverables must be received no later than December 15, 2026, approximately eight weeks after contract award.

title: X-ray Diffraction System (XRD)
description: This Contract will procure and install a high-resolution X-ray diffractometry (HR-XRD) system for use in the Epitaxy facilities at the National Research Council Canada (NRC). This HR-XRD system will provide critical feedback for the growth of III-V semiconductor heterostructures grown epitaxially. These systems are used for research and commercial growth of III-V semiconductors (arsenides, antimonides, and phosphides). These systems grow demanding heterostructures for a wide range of optoelectronic and quantum applications, such as: quantum dot lasers, InP-based nanowire quantum dots for single-photon emission, quantum cascade and interband cascade lasers, and GaSb-based diode lasers incorporating quaternary and quinary alloys.

title: E6HAL-230009 RFI Socio-economic Catering
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) intends to compile a list of underrepresented suppliers that can deliver catering services in the Atlantic Region. The list will be shared within federal departments and agencies in Atlantic Canada so that employees can use the list for their catering needs. To be eligible to participate: the principal place of business must be in Canada; your business must be owned by a member of an underrepresented group, which includes: women, visible minorities, persons with disabilities, and members of the 2SLGBTQQIA+ community (as per Annex A: Supplier Diversity Program Forms); and be able to provide catering services in at least one of the four provinces in the Atlantic Region (New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia, Newfoundland and Labrador) To submit the required information for this opportunity complete the form at the following link: https://forms-formulaires.alpha.canada.ca/en/id/cmer94nwg012fyr01artk8l6c Once received, we will follow up to confirm if you are eligible. Please be advised that inclusion on the list is not a guarantee that your business will be contacted to provide services. For any questions or comments on this pilot project, please contact pwgsc.basatlantic-scaatlantiquetpsgc@tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca.

title: E6HAL-230008 Pilot Project for Indigenous Artists
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) has launched a pilot project to compile a list of emerging, mid-career, and established professional Indigenous artists in the Atlantic Region. The list will be shared within federal departments and agencies in Atlantic Canada so that employees can use the list to procure Indigenous art for use in Government of Canada buildings and offices in New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. This opportunity is open to emerging, mid-career, or established Indigenous artists and artisans who create art or traditional crafts representative of the Indigenous Peoples in Atlantic Canada. To submit the required information for this opportunity complete the Indigenous Artist Form at the following link: https://forms-formulaires.alpha.canada.ca/en/id/cmc1xkjh8001ex601pjp4kwcj Once received, we will follow up to confirm if you are eligible. Please be advised that inclusion on the list is not a guarantee that your business will be contacted to provide services. For questions or comments, please contact mailto:pwgsc.basatlantic-scaatlantiquetpsgc@tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca

title: W8472-225864 Dive Tender Replacement Project RFI
description: Canada, as represented by the Department of National Defence (DND), with the assistance of Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC), has issued this RFI on the Dive Tender Replacement (DTR) project. This RFI is seeking Industry feedback regarding potential solutions which meet the Dive Tender Replacement project operational requirements as listed in Annex A provided herewith. The DTR build requirement is anticipated to fall under the small vessel construction component, Pillar 2, of the National Shipbuilding Strategy (NSS). Restrictions-on-bidding provisions may therefore, apply to the shipyards selected by Canada under Pillar 1 of the NSS. The Royal Canadian Navy (RCN) currently uses an existing fleet of Granby and Sechelt-class vessels to support divers in completing underwater tasks that are essential to naval operations and public safety. The new vessels aim to replace the existing fleet of Granby and Sechelt-class vessels, to facilitate the full range of diving operations and will resemble traditional 24-crew diving support vessels.

title: 26Z5AR6 - REPLACE INTERIOR FINISH
description: Statement of Work Federal Bureau of Prisons Federal Correctional Institution (FCI) Bastrop, Texas Project # 26Z5AR6 Replace Interior Finish 1. SPECIFICATIONS: A. INTRODUCTION The Federal Correctional Institution at Bastrop, located at 1341 Highway 95 North, Bastrop, TX 78602, has identified four (4) buildings with severe interior damage resulting from prolonged water intrusion caused by long-term roof leaks. The continued moisture exposure has resulted in deterioration of gypsum wall systems, ceiling assemblies, suspended ceiling systems, and wood paneling. These conditions may present unsanitary and potentially hazardous conditions, including the possible presence of microbial growth and other hazardous materials. Abatement is required to protect occupant health and prepare the spaces for future restoration. The Contractor is strongly encouraged to attend the pre-bid site visit identified in the solicitation, to assess existing conditions that may affect performance of contract work. *8/18/2026 - WAGE DETERMINATION FOR BASTROP COUNTY, TX HAS BEEN ADDED IN THE ATTACHMENTS SECTION. **There will be a site visit at FCI Bastrop, 1341 Highway 95 N, Bastrop, TX 77868 on Wednesday, August 26th at 1:00 PM CST. If you wish to attend, please email the points of contact in the solicitation and include background check paperwork for everyone wishing to enter available in the attachments section. Please do not digitally sign your name on the background check form, a physical wet signature is required. Background check paperwork is due on Thursday, August 20th at 1:00 PM CST. Please have a valid state of federal ID. B. The Contractor will be required to comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, including OSHA, EPA, and BOP safety, health, and security requirements. 2. Work shall be conducted in a manner that protects staff, inmates, visitors, and adjacent occupied spaces. C.1 Hazardous Material and Environmental Compliance C.1.1 General 1. Due to the age of the buildings and the duration of water intrusion, hazardous materials may be present, including but not limited to: - Mold or microbial contamination -Lead-based paint -Asbestos-Containing Materials (ACM) -Other regulated building materials. 2. The Contractor shall comply with all applicable requirements of OSHA, EPA and any other government regulatory agencies. C.1.2 Mold and Microbial Contamination 1. The contractor shall implement appropriate engineering controls, including containment and negative air pressure with HEPA filtration, when removing materials impacted by mold or suspected microbial growth. 2. Removal shall be performed to a point of clean, sound, and dry substrate. 3. Remaining surfaces shall be HEPA-vacuumed and cleaned in accordance with industry-recognized remediation practices. 4. The Contractor shall take reasonable measures to prevent cross-contamination during abatement. C.1.3 Lead-Based Paint 1. Due to the age of the buildings, painted surfaces disturbed during demolition may contain lead-based paint. 2. The Contractor shall perform work in accordance with applicable OSHA and EPA lead safety standards. 3. The Contractor shall implement appropriate worker protection and dust control measures. C.1.4 Asbestos-Containing Materials 1. The Government has conducted asbestos surveys of suspected building materials within the identified work areas. Testing was performed on materials reasonably suspected to contain asbestos, and the Government maintains documentation of all sampling results. 2. Based on testing performed to date, materials identified for removal under this Statement of Work are not known to contain asbestos. 3. If the Contractor encounters any material that differs from identified building material to be removed, the Contractor shall immediately stop work in the affected area and notify the COR prior to disturbing the material. 4. No material suspected of containing asbestos shall be disturbed, removed, or handled until the COR and FCI Bastrop Occupational Health & Safety Department staff have been consulted. 5. Failure to consult with the COR prior to disturbing questionable material may result in liability for unauthorized disturbance of regulated materials. C.2 CONTAINMENT AND PROTECTION 1. The Contractor shall provide dust, debris, and hazard containment using polyethylene barriers, negative air machines, and HEPA filtration as required. 2. Adjacent occupied spaces, mechanical systems, and finishes shall be protected from contamination. 3. The contractor shall always maintain safe and secure egress routes. Remove and dispose of approximately 5,500 square feet of gypsum ceiling systems, including associated framing and insulation where damaged. 3. Suspended Ceilings a. Remove and dispose of approximately 1,100 square feet of suspended ceiling systems, including tiles, grid, hangers, and supports impacted by moisture. 4. Wood Paneling a. Remove and dispose of approximately 1,200 square feet of water-damaged wood paneling, including furring strips and fasteners. title: Q4 FY26 Baltimore Harbor and Channels Maintenance Dredging, Maryland Channels, Chesapeake Bay, MD
description: **Amendment 0001 Key Changes Summary: Milestone Extensions:-ProjNet RFI Cutoff: Extended to 13 August 2026, 10:00 AM EDT (originally 03 August).-Bid Submission Deadline: Extended to 01 September 2026, 10:00 AM EDT (originally 25 August).-Virtual Bid Opening: Rescheduled to 01 September 2026, 11:00 AM EDT (originally 25 August).Geotechnical and Sediment Data:-Incorporates four (4) sediment reports for: Craighill Entrance, Craighill Angle, Craighill Upper Range, and Cutoff Angle.-Clarifies that geotechnical data is unavailable and will not be provided for Curtis Bay and Brewerton Angle. Plan Sheet Revisions:-Sheet V116 (Coordinates): Removes F1 from the Dredge Area Coordinates box and updates the coordinates for points F1 and F9.Sheet V112 (Poplar Island): Adds Inflow Point 8 to the Poplar Island drawings. **END Amendment 0001 Key Changes Summary****The project consists of maintenance dredging approximately 2,250,000 cubic yards (cy) from the deep-draft federal navigation channels serving the Port of Baltimore. The work is to be performed between November 2026 through March 2027. The dredging depth for all channels is 50 feet mean lower low water (ft MLLW) with an additional 1 ? 2 foot of allowable overdepth. Approximately 1,538,000 cy will be dredged from the Maryland approach channels (Craighill Entrance, Craighill Angle, Cutoff Angle, and Upper Range Channels) and placed at the Paul S. Sarbanes Ecosystems Restoration Project at Poplar Island. Approximately 700,000 cy will be dredged from Baltimore Harbor Channels (Brewerton Angle and Curtis Bay Channels) and placed at the Cox Creek Dredged Material Containment Facility. The work areas are within heavy commercial waterways supporting the Port of Baltimore. The equipment required for this work commonly consists of two 30 plus cubic yard clamshell dredges, one 24 ? 30-inch hydraulic unloader, six to eight large tugs, six to eight 2,500 ? 6,000 cubic yard material scows, a drag bar and barge, and appropriate attendant plant and pipeline. The material will be dredged by clamshell/bucket and scow and placed within a period of performance of approximately 120 calendar days from receipt of Notice-to-Proceed.

title: Sources Sought � Motorola GTR 8000 Land Mobile Radio (LMR) System with OCONUS Installation in Japan
description: 1.0 Introduction and Market Research Transparency This is a Sources Sought Notice issued by Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Yokosuka for market research and planning purposes only. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Government is in the final phase of its market research for this requirement. Previous Requests for Information (RFIs) have been posted to the GSA eBuy and NASA SEWP portals. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to identify the full scope of capable vendors on the unrestricted open market. The Government is specifically seeking to identify all qualified sources able to provide this complete solution (hardware and services) as an Open Market requirement. 2.0 Requirement Overview NAVSUP FLC Yokosuka is seeking to identify capable vendors who can provide both the brand-name hardware and the complex OCONUS installation services for a Motorola GTR 8000 Land Mobile Radio (LMR) System. 2.1. Hardware and Core Services Requirement: Vendors must be capable of providing the following list of equipment and associated installation/programming services: 2.1.1. One (1) Lot of Equipment to include: Two (2) GTR Repeaters, Three (3) GTR Basestations, Antennas, and Miscellaneous Hardware required for installation 2.1.2. One (1) Lot of Implementation and System Optimization services 2.1.3. One hundred twenty-four (124) PORTABLE RADIO APX6000 VHF MHZ MODEL 2.5 (H98KGF9PW6BN) 2.1.4. One hundred twenty-four (124) ADD: PROGRAMMING OVER P25 (OTAP) (G996) 2.1.5. One hundred twenty-four (124) ADD: SINGLE UNIT PACKING (H842) 2.1.6. One hundred twenty-four (124) ADD: CONVENTIONAL OPERATION (H35) 2.1.7. One hundred twenty-four (124) ADD: BASELINE RELEASE SW (QA09113) 2.1.8. One hundred twenty-four (124) ADD: 5Y ESSENTIAL ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE (HA00025AH) 2.1.9. One hundred twenty-four (124) ADD: ASTRO DIGITAL CAI OPERATION (Q806) 2.1.10. One hundred twenty-four (124) SOFTWARE LICENSE ENH: AES ENCRYPTION AND ADP (Q629) 2.1.11. One hundred twenty-four (124) ALT: BATT IMPRES 2 LIION TIA4950 R IP68 3100T (QA07578) 2.1.12. One hundred twenty-four (124) SOFTWARE LICENSE ENH: SUBMERSIBLE (DELTA T) (H499) 2.1.13. Fifty (50) Portable Radio Battery Impres 2 Li-Ion TIA4950 R IP68 3100T (PMNN4547A) 2.1.14. Fifty (50) Portable Antenna, Helical Whip, GPS, 136-174 MHZ (NAR6593A) 2.1.15. One hundred forty-four (144) Charger TAA, Desktop Single Unit Impres 2, US Plug (NNTN8860ATAA) 2.1.16. One hundred twenty-four (124) Device Programming services for all APX 6000 Radios (LSV00Q00202A) 2.2. OCONUS Installation Requirement (Logistical Assumptions): 2.2.1. The Contractor shall be responsible for the complete on-site installation, programming, and system optimization at a designated U.S. Navy operational site in Japan, which shall be a remote island. 2.2.2. For quoting purposes, please use the following logistical assumptions: 2.2.2.1. Travel to Japan: The Contractor is responsible for all costs associated with travel, lodging, and per diem to reach mainland Japan (staging area). 2.2.2.2. Local Transit: The U.S. Navy will assist with the final transportation of personnel and equipment from the mainland staging area to the final designated installation site. 2.2.2.3. Site Support: The U.S. Navy will provide lodging and meals at the final designated installation site. 2.2.2.4. Clearances: Contractor personnel must be eligible for SOFA status and SPOT processing for base access. 3.0 Information Requested from Vendors Interested and capable open-market vendors are requested to provide a brief capability statement (not to exceed 5 pages) addressing the following: 3.1. Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, Unique Entity ID (UEI), and Point of Contact (Name, Email, Phone). 3.2. Business Size: Please state your business size and any socio-economic statuses under NAICS Code 334220. 3.3. Technical Capability & Partnership: A statement confirming your company's status as an authorized Motorola partner/reseller and your capability to perform all required OCONUS services as described in Section 2.0. Please briefly describe your experience with similar projects. 3.4. Contracting Approach: Please confirm that your company is willing and able to quote this entire requirement (hardware and services) as an Open Market procurement. 4.0 Submission Instructions This is an RFI for market research purposes only. No award will be made from this posting. The Government will not pay for information received. Responses should be submitted via email to Jon R. Miller at jon.miller30.ln@us.navy.mil no later than Tuesday, 1 September 2026, 11:00 PM JST].

The continued moisture exposure has resulted in deterioration of gypsum wall systems, ceiling assemblies, suspended ceiling systems, and wood paneling. The Contractor will be required to comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, including OSHA, EPA, and BOP safety, health, and security requirements. 2. Due to the age of the buildings and the duration of water intrusion, hazardous materials may be present, including but not limited to: - Mold or microbial contamination -Lead-based paint -Asbestos-Containing Materials (ACM) -Other regulated building materials. 2. The Contractor shall comply with all applicable requirements of OSHA, EPA and any other government regulatory agencies. C.1.2 Mold and Microbial Contamination 1. description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 5.101(d). This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12-1NMP-26-B-0020 is issued as an invitation for bid (IFB) for various Oil, Dry Bean, Fortified Milled Rice, Peas, Lentils and Corn-Soy Blend Plus products for use in International Food Assistance Programs. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). description: This is a solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes only solicitation. Basis for Award The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation represents the best value to the Government, price and other factors considered, utilizing the best value trade-off process. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: Technical Capability, Past Performance, and Price. Technical Capability: The Government will evaluate the offeror�s technical capability to perform the requirements outlined in the Statement of Work (SOW). This includes the offeror�s ability to perform secure document destruction services, ability to provide Certificates of Destruction and other documentation, and comply with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations. The evaluation will consider the offeror�s approach to perform certified services for various work order requirements including their understanding of the scope, tasks, and performance standards, such as maintaining a secure chain of custody and utilizing high-security shredding mechanisms. Proposals must demonstrate a clear and comprehensive plan for fulfilling all contract requirements. Past Performance: The Government will assess the offeror�s past performance in performing shredding services to federal, state, or local government agencies, or commercial entities. The evaluation will consider the quality, timeliness, and reliability of previous contract performance, as determined through references or other available information. Offerors with a proven record of successful performance on contracts of similar size, scope, and complexity will be viewed more favorably. Price: Price will be evaluated based on the total proposed Firm Fixed Price for all labor, materials, equipment, and services required to fulfill the SOW. The Government will consider whether the price is fair and reasonable in relation to the technical capability and past performance of the offeror. While price is an important factor, it will be considered in conjunction with the non-price evaluation criteria to determine the overall best value to the Government. A quote must comply in all aspects with the requirements and conditions set forth in this RFQ; a quote must meet or exceed all mandatory RFQ requirements. If an Offeror takes exception to any of the terms and conditions of the RFQ or fails to meet any of the requirements of the RFQ, then the Government may consider the quote unacceptable. A Firm-Fixed Price contract will be awarded to the responsible offeror whose offer fully conforms to this solicitation and is determined to be the most advantageous, considering price and other factors. The Government intends to evaluate offers and award a contract without discussions with Offerors. Therefore, the Offeror�s initial offer should contain the Offeror�s best terms. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions, if necessary. The Government may reject any or all offers if such action is in the public interest, accept other than the lowest offer, and waive informalities and minor irregularities in offers received. The anticipated award date is 10 days after solicitation closing date. Only one purchase order is anticipated resulting from this RFQ, however the Government reserves the right to withdraw, modify, or eliminate various aspects of the requirement determined to be too costly or impractical prior to award. title: Granite Table inspection, calibration, and lapping/repair
description: This is a Sources Sought only. You MUST send e-mail to the POC (heather.j.petersen.civ@army.mil) that includes the following: 1) Company Name 2) Cage Code or EUI number 3) company POC, e-mail address, and phone number 4) capability statement that outlines you have and can complete the work outlined below. ___________________ Scope of Work (SOW) 1. Purpose: The purpose of this Scope of Work (SOW) is to define a performance-based specification to calibrate granite surface tables for the Rock Island Arsenal's Joint Manufacturing and Technology Center (JMTC). The work shall be performed by an ISO 17025 accredited vendor shall include the inspection, calibration, and lapping/repair of the tabletops of any that are not within specification. 2. Invoices for services must include a breakout of all costs and must be submitted to the JMTC Representative for review and concurance after services are completed. This is to verify that the invoices are in line with the contract prices and JTR approved prices. 3. Performance Period: Contractor�s effort will begin immediately after Contract/Task Order award. This will be for a Base year and Four Option Years for a total of five years. 4. Detailed Specifications: Rock Island Arsenal's JMTC includes the list of granite tables covered by this SOW and is represented below. Laboratory Grade AA 36A R-68-1439 48 X 96 36A 19567-M 60 X 120 36F R-82-791 60 X 96 36F 22387-M 48 X 72 36F RIA30627 48 X 96 36S 19583-M 48 X 96 Laboratory Grade A 40A 19587-M 48 X 108 40A 19589-M 48 X 108 40B R-86-1412 72 X 120 40C 22487-M 48 X 96 40C R-85-3474 72 X 120 40C RIA31418 72 X 120 40C R-86-948 96 X 144 40M R-59-304 48 X 96 40R R-85-3475 72 X 120 40W 23415-M 72 X 120 299 R-85-3565 48 X 72 299 P-9299 48 X 72 4.1 Per ASME B89.3.7 the ISO 17025 accredited contractor shall inspect the granite surface plates and determine both its overall and local flatness. If necessary, the contractor will lap the working surface back to within specification standards. 4.2 Calibration and any necessary lapping shall be performed on an annual basis. 4.3 After the granite surface plate has been calibrated, the contractor shall affix a calibration sticker to the granite surface plate and provide a Service Acceptance Report (SAR) to the JMTC Representative within three (3) business days of completing the calibration. 5. Working Hours: 0600-1430 hours, Monday-Friday, Government Holidays excluded, unless otherwise authorized, and agreed upon, prior to deviation of the work schedule. 6. Security: The RIA-JMTC is an Army installation subject to Department of Defense safeguards, various precautions, and plant protection measures. At all times during the execution of this SOW, the contractor will maintain adequate plant protection devices to minimize espionage, sabotage, and other malicious destruction and damage. The contractor shall comply with all security requirements of the Rock Island Arsenal. 7. Final acceptance inspection shall be performed by the JMTC Representative to verify that all requirements of this SOW (and any modifications thereto) are satisfied.

title: J065--Intent to Sole Source - Omnicell Service Agreement
description: Intent to Sole Source Omnicell, Inc. VAMC Palo Alto Health Care System Support Services Renewal Procurement Type: Open Market (Non-FSS) Period of Performance: September 1, 2026 July 31, 2027 Estimated Value: $324,618.25 (Grand Total) The Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Palo Alto Health Care System (VAPAHCS), intends to award a sole source contract to Omnicell, Inc., the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and sole provider of proprietary Support Services for Omnicell automated supply dispensing equipment across the Palo Alto campus. The required Support Services beginning September 1, 2026, through July 31, 2027, billed monthly, and include OEM support for multiple Omnicell XT and AUX Supply dispensing systems. These services consist of OEM maintenance, software license support, remote server access components, and proprietary modules not offered under Omnicell s Federal Supply Schedule. The quote notes that continuation of Support Services requires an open market purchase order, as the items are not available under Omnicell s FSS contract. Omnicell is the only source capable of providing these services due to exclusive OEM control over software, firmware, hardware components, server access keys, and certified maintenance. No authorized third party providers exist with the ability to service or maintain the XT series supply dispensing systems. Service gaps would result in reinstatement fees and risk operational disruption as noted in the manufacturer s renewal documentation. Instructions for Interested Respondents Although the VA intends to solicit and negotiate solely with Omnicell, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government s proprietary requirement may submit a capability statement. Responses must, at minimum, address the following questions and include supporting documentation: Required Questions for Respondents: Can your company provide OEM equivalent maintenance, support, software updates, and proprietary license coverage for Omnicell XT and AUX Supply automated dispensing systems? Can your company demonstrate authorization from Omnicell to service, support, or maintain these systems, including access to proprietary firmware, licenses, and server integration components? title: Phenom Pharos G2 desktop model scanning electron microscope (SEM)
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention intends to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order to Nanoscience Instruments for purchase of Phenom Pharos G2 desktop model scanning electron microscope (SEM) with field emission electron beam source and an energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) detector capable of elemental mapping. There are two types of beams, field emission and tungsten filament. Traditional tungsten filaments are limited to approximately 250,000x magnification whereas a field emission source can achieve up to 8 times greater resolution (up to 2,000,000x magnification), which permits imaging particles with sizes of just a few nanometers. As such, the 2 key requirements for this procurement are a field emission electron beam source and elemental mapping capability. Only the Phenom Pharos G2 desktop scanning electron microscope (SEM) with field emission electron beam source and an energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) detector capable of elemental mapping sold by Nanoscience Instruments, Inc. meets both these requirements. This contract action is for supplies and/or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 13.101(b) (SAP). BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency has a requirement for a Contractor to rehabilitate the roadway and parking area within the Day Use Area of Pingo Canadian Landmark. The work includes restoring road width and profile, improving sightlines and RV clearance, stabilizing soft subgrade conditions with geotextile and granular fill as required, re-establishing parking lot edges, and improving drainage throughout the site. The project also includes grading and placement of a gravel surface course to provide a safe, smooth, and well-drained driving surface for visitors. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than October 15, 2026. COMPREHENSIVE LAND CLAIMS AGREEMENT This procurement is subject to the following comprehensive Land Claims Agreement(s): • Inuvialuit Final Agreement SET-ASIDE UNDER THE PROCUREMENT STRATEGY FOR INDIGENOUS BUSINESS This procurement is set aside under the federal government’s Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) as detailed in Annex 9.4 of the Supply Manual entitled “Requirements for the Set-Aside Program for Indigenous Business”. In order to be considered, a bidder must certify that it qualifies as an Indigenous business as defined under PSIB and that it will comply with all requirements of PSIB. If no bidder meets the qualifications as an Indigenous business defined under PSIB and all its requirements, PCA reserves the right to cancel the solicitation and re-issue with an open competitive solicitation process. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: USACE SPK Construction - Natomas PP5, Sacramento, CA
description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) is issuing a solicitation for the requirement to construct a new pumping plant facility in Sacramento, CA. The American River Common Features, Natomas Basin Project was authorized by the Water Resources Reform Development Act of 2014. The Natomas Basin is divided into nine reaches, A through I. RD-1000?s Pumping Plant 5 (PP5) is in Reach B, located along the Sacramento River near the landside toe of the levee and south of Interstate 5. PP5 is designed to discharge drainage from the West Drainage Canal to the Sacramento River following any significant amount of rainfall. The existing PP5 is in the path of completing the Reach B levee improvements that includes seepage berm, adjacent levee, and raising discharge pipes above the 200-year water surface elevation. The existing PP5 will be demolished, and a new facility will be constructed about 300 feet up the canal to allow for the levee features to be constructed .Point of Contact: Antonina Beal, Contract Specialist. Email: Antonina.Beal@usace.army.mil. Please refer to the full solicitation document for all detailed instructions, clauses, and submission requirements.

title: USACE SPK Construction - Natomas PP5, Sacramento, CA
description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) is issuing a solicitation for the requirement to construct a new pumping plant facility in Sacramento, CA. The American River Common Features, Natomas Basin Project was authorized by the Water Resources Reform Development Act of 2014. The Natomas Basin is divided into nine reaches, A through I. RD-1000?s Pumping Plant 5 (PP5) is in Reach B, located along the Sacramento River near the landside toe of the levee and south of Interstate 5. PP5 is designed to discharge drainage from the West Drainage Canal to the Sacramento River following any significant amount of rainfall. The existing PP5 is in the path of completing the Reach B levee improvements that includes seepage berm, adjacent levee, and raising discharge pipes above the 200-year water surface elevation. The existing PP5 will be demolished, and a new facility will be constructed about 300 feet up the canal to allow for the levee features to be constructed .Point of Contact: Antonina Beal, Contract Specialist. Email: Antonina.Beal@usace.army.mil. Please refer to the full solicitation document for all detailed instructions, clauses, and submission requirements.

title: Harry S Truman Streetscape Perimeter Construction Project
description: The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS) New England Region, Acquisition Management Division intends to hire a construction contractor to implement and enhance security and esthetics for the area around the Harry S Truman (HST) Streetscape Construction building located in Washington DC. The project originated in response to the events of 9/11 where high-profile government buildings were targeted by terrorists. This major renovation project will replace the temporary security measures surrounding the building to provide countermeasures that will secure the building, protect employees and visitors, and improve the surrounding streetscape by creating an attractive and accessible environment for pedestrians. Once complete, the temporary security measures will be replaced with tested and proven countermeasures that will secure the building, protect employees and visitors, and improve the surrounding streetscape by creating an attractive and accessible environment for pedestrians. The project involves civil/site construction of approximately 162,000 square feet of streetscape (sidewalks, curb & gutter, utilities, etc.), requiring 4 phases for completion. title: Harry S Truman Streetscape Perimeter Construction Project
description: The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS) New England Region, Acquisition Management Division intends to hire a construction contractor to implement and enhance security and esthetics for the area around the Harry S Truman (HST) Streetscape Construction building located in Washington DC. The project originated in response to the events of 9/11 where high-profile government buildings were targeted by terrorists. This major renovation project will replace the temporary security measures surrounding the building to provide countermeasures that will secure the building, protect employees and visitors, and improve the surrounding streetscape by creating an attractive and accessible environment for pedestrians. Once complete, the temporary security measures will be replaced with tested and proven countermeasures that will secure the building, protect employees and visitors, and improve the surrounding streetscape by creating an attractive and accessible environment for pedestrians. The project involves civil/site construction of approximately 162,000 square feet of streetscape (sidewalks, curb & gutter, utilities, etc.), requiring 4 phases for completion. title: Lab Waste Piping CIPP
description: THIS IS A COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION FOR COMMERCIAL ITEMS PREPARED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE FORMAT IN REVOLUTIONARY FAR OVERHAUL (RFO) 12.201-1 SIMPLIFIED PROCEDURES. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONSTITUTES THE ONLY SOLICITATION; QUOTATIONS ARE BEING REQUESTED, AND A SEPARATE WRITTEN SOLICITATION DOCUMENT WILL NOT BE ISSUED. THE SOLICITATION IS BEING ISSUED USING SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION PROCEDURES UNDER THE AUTHORITY OF RFO 12. The solicitation number is 1333ND26QNB190526 and is a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 dated March 13, 2026. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 238220 � Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors with a small business size standard of $19.0M. Performance and Payment bonds will be required. This acquisition is being solicited as a 100% small business set-aside. BACKGROUND: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is a government scientific research facility located in Gaithersburg, MD. The facility buildings largely date to the early 1960�s. A previous CIPP project found cracked and split cast iron laboratory waste piping in the under-floor utility trench in buildings 223 and 226. Subsequently, NIST Shops have reported leaking piping in building 224. Generally, due to the video surveillance in both previous project buildings, it is accepted that this 60-year-old piping shares the same general condition of having long linear cracks and complete axial splitting. The under-floor trench space is considered to be a confined space. This requirement is to utilize Cure in Place Pipe (CIPP) to conduct the repair to the 224 laboratory waste piping. title: Electrical Rebuild, Black Rock Lake Dam, Thomaston, Connecticut
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is solicitating an Invitation for Bids (IFB) for Electrical Feeder Upgrades at the Black Rock Lake Dam in Thomaston, Connecticut. This will be a 100% Small Business Set-Aside IFB procurement. The NAICS code for the work described below is 238210 with a size standard of $19M. The project is planned to be issued in July 2026 and will be set aside for Small Businesses. The period of performance will be approximately 180 days. The estimated magnitude of this project is between $750,000 and $1,250,000.The work of this project involves electrical feeder upgrades at the Black Rock Lake Dam in Thomaston, Connecticut. Specific work tasks include, but are not limited to, replacing the existing overhead dam feeder (which runs underneath a high voltage line) from the project office to a designated manhole with a buried conduit duct bank.The existing gate tower feeder is in an existing buried duct bank which runs up the dam face and in exposed conduit beneath the gate tower bridge will be removed and replaced with new. The fused disconnect at the existing overhead line end will be removed. The existing manual transfer switches in the gate tower and project office will be removed. The existing 480V Panel-A, transformer, and 120/208 Panel-B in the gate tower will be removed and replaced with new. The existing service entrance circuit breaker and its enclosure will remain and be reused. Install new propane genset in the project office parking lot. Install a new propane tank with an underground propane line connected to the genset. The new genset will be sized to power both the project office and the gate tower on loss of utility. The propane tank will be sized to provide 5 days of run time before needing to be refilled. Install a new properly sized automatic transfer switch to feed existing panel MDP-1 from either the existing utility feeder or the new propane genset.

title: 355 CMS Fuel Compressors Maintenance
description: The 355 Contracting Squadron is requesting a long term service contract to maintain and repair Quincy Air Compressors (See attached PWS for Models). This compressor is essential for daily squadron operations, including vehicle maintenance and repairs for two Quincy air compressors and a desiccant air dryer at Davis-Monthan AFB. These systems supply vital breathing and shop air for the 355th Component Maintenance Squadron (355 CMS). The contractor shall inspect and perform preventive maintenance, as recommended by the manufacturer, on the Quincy air compressors and desiccant air dryer. At a minimum, this includes changing filters and separators, changing oil, inspecting and servicing valves and controls, taking oil samples, verifying proper operation of safety devices, and conducting operational checks of the compressors and dryer. The contractor shall ensure the system operates properly and safely while minimizing disruptions and inconveniences to users until the next scheduled maintenance. Repairs made during scheduled preventive maintenance are considered any repairs consistent with normal wear and tear of compressor and dryer operation. If the contractor identifies conditions that require work beyond normal preventive maintenance, the contractor shall treat that work as non-routine maintenance and proceed in accordance with the PWS.

title: Intrinsic Market Resilience (IMR) Proposers Day
description: The evolution of markets from physical trading floors to interconnected, electronic venues has introduced new speed, transparency, and efficiency, but has also created new attack surfaces and systemic risks. Modern markets, which host trading for everything from equities and bonds to energy and cloud computing resources, can be manipulated in ways unanticipated by their designers. The 2010 United States Equity market "flash crash" and the 2000-2001 California energy crisis demonstrated how weaknesses in a market's public interfaces could have dramatic consequences. Similar design issues in today's complex, interacting market systems could be used to cause economic damage, which the IMR program technology seeks to prevent. The IMR program aims to develop repair methods to protect essential economic sectors against devastating attacks that exploit the public interfaces of modern markets. Current legal and regulatory protections focus on deterring profit-seeking manipulation and ensuring compliance, but they do not sufficiently protect markets from adversaries aiming simply to cause disruption. The IMR program seeks to address this gap by developing the tools to automatically model market designs, identify hidden weaknesses, and recommend and analyze repairs on the market models to make markets fundamentally more resilient to attack. IMR aims to combine Large Language Model (LLM)-based automation with rigorous modeling and analysis to identify remediations for market weaknesses. The program will develop formal notations to precisely describe how markets operate and coordinate, creating machine-analyzable models from informal descriptions like regulatory filings and technical specifications. Against these models, IMR will formulate and assess "resilience conjectures� - mathematical statements about desirable market properties, such as the inability for actors to manipulate prices without risking loss. By automatically analyzing these conjectures, the program aims to prove that a market design is resilient in specific ways or, if it is not, to generate a counterexample that illustrates a concrete weakness. These counterexamples will then be used to refine the conjectures and, ultimately, to recommend and confirm specific repairs to the market's design. This approach is intended to provide a capability to protect U.S. markets against adversaries who wish to cause chaos, ensuring the stability of both civilian and military critical resources that rely on modern market mechanisms.
